Subject: Initial checklist + two questions on custody and enclaves

Hi Vanessa / Marissa —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As we scope the EU + Japan pilot for Cardinal Banking, a couple of operational items came up that we want to lock before the architecture call on Friday:

1) Key custody: For the APAC POA we need to confirm whether Redwood will host customer keys in a regional HSM or whether the SI (Kitebridge) will operate an HSM inside the customer VPC. Cardinal has strict obligations that keys never leave JP.

2) Enclave hosting: On the call we talked about a private inference enclave for sensitive PII. Do you have a standard addendum for enclave hosting and access controls (audit log cadence, operator roles)?

I've attached our initial DataCustody checklist and a draft addendum that Cardinal's legal put together — it's deliberately conservative. Can you flag rows we can't accept or need to change before we share with the customer?

Proposed next step: 30m sync Thursday 10:00 CET to map responsibilities and agree a minimal set of controls for the PoC.

Cheers,
Lucas
Head of Integrations — Kitebridge Consulting

Attachments: DataCustody-Checklist.xlsx, Draft-Addendum-v1.docx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:02:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Initial checklist + two questions on custody and enclaves

Hi Lucas —

Thanks for sending this through and for the checklist — helpful. Quick answers upfront so you can prep Cardinal's legal team:

- Key custody: Redwood's standard hosted option stores KMS keys in the region where the private deployment is provisioned. For JP we can provision a regional HSM-backed KMS, but we also support an SI-managed KMS in-customer if the customer requires exclusive key control. There are tradeoffs: SI-managed KMS requires network peering and an agreed key-rotation ops runbook.

- Enclave hosting: We do have a standard enclave addendum but it is usually adapted per-customer. The addendum covers operator roles, audit log retention (default 90 days, can be extended), and emergency access procedures. We typically surface a minimal set of controls for PoC and defer hardening to the production roll.

Action items:
- Marissa: can you scan the attached addendum and mark any absolute no-ops for Redwood?
- Sergio: can you confirm whether our JP region supports HSM KMS provisioning this week (it did in QA last sprint but want prod confirmation)?
- Karthik: please draft a short ops-runbook snippet for SI-managed KMS (network, rotation, revocation).

Thursday 10:00 CET works for me — invite sent.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Market Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Lucas Moretti <lucas.moretti@kitebridge.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T14:27:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Initial checklist + two questions on custody and enclaves

Vanessa / Lucas —

I've reviewed the draft addendum at a high level. A couple of notes:

- Key export prohibition: We can accept language that keys "must not be exported outside JP/EU" provided the customer understands that Redwood will need a recovery key escrow mechanism for disaster recovery; we usually propose a three-way escrow (customer, Redwood, SI) with split-key encryption. If the customer insists on single-party control with zero escrow, that's an SI-managed KMS only and we will require a SOC-2 Type II report from the SI and annual key-rotation attestation.

- Audit logs: 90 days is our default. For regulated customers we can extend to 365 days at an add-on cost; must be ordered as part of Dedicated or Private.

- Incident response: propose a 48-hour initial notification SLA and joint triage within 72 hours for confirmed breaches.

I flagged the redlines inline and saved them as comments in Draft-Addendum-v1.docx.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Lucas / team —

Quick infra confirmation: JP production region can provision HSM-backed KMS. Lead ops will need a maintenance window to install the HSM stack (we estimate 4 hours). For a PoC we can spin up a dedicated subnet in the customer's VPC and peer it to our private control plane; that removes cross-border flows.

Notes for Friday's call:
- We need to agree a heartbeat and monitoring integration (CloudWatch / Stackdriver / Prometheus depending on customer).
- If the SI runs the KMS, we require an agreed revocation API and an onboarding checklist for operator MFA and attestation.

I'll bring a short diagram and a runbook snippet.

-Sergio
Partner Solutions Engineering

Subject: Re: Initial checklist + two questions on custody and enclaves

Thanks all —

This is helpful and addresses our immediate concerns. Cardinal confirms they will accept a three-way escrow model for the PoC (customer + Redwood + Kitebridge) and will compile the signed SOC-2 report for Kitebridge before access. They asked us to capture a short list of must-haves for the PoC:

- Keys must be provisioned in JP region HSM for inference sessions touching account numbers.
- Enclave access must be recorded and retained 180 days for the pilot (Cardinal will accept 180 for PoC).
- Joint incident triage SLA (48h notify, 72h triage).

We will sign the addendum with the redlines Marissa suggested and return a signed PDF by end of week.

See you on the call Thursday 10:00 CET / 18:00 JST.

Best,
Yumi Sato
Engagement Lead — Kitebridge (Japan)
